items.title: Vienna Sees Rare November Snow
items.gist: A heavy snowfall turned Vienna’s streets white and disrupted travel across Austria. The snow was striking, but the road and rail delays were serious.
items.summary: Vienna recorded its heaviest November snowfall in more than 40 years. The Hohe Warte weather station measured 17 centimetres on Thursday. Snow and icy roads caused crashes and delays in several regions. The A21 motorway was closed for hours after vehicles became stuck. Vienna Airport also reported some delays while planes were de-iced. Forecasters expected cold weather to keep snow on the ground.
items.host_open: Vienna got a winter postcard, along with a traffic headache. What was your experience of the snow?

items.title: ORF Approves A Loss-Making Budget
items.gist: Austria’s public broadcaster has approved a budget that plans a large loss next year. Managers say they must save money, while critics warn about the impact on staff and programmes.
items.summary: The ORF supervisory board approved its 2027 budget on Thursday. The plan expects the broadcaster to have a loss of more than 30 million euros. The ORF says it will receive 93 million euros less each year after a government funding change. It plans to reduce its workforce by 350 to 380 full-time jobs by the end of 2029. The ORF says it wants viewers to feel as little effect as possible on programmes. Political critics disagree about how the broadcaster should make savings.
items.host_open: A public broadcaster’s budget is also a debate about what viewers get. How does this look from Austria?

items.title: Austrian Donations Reach €1.08 Billion
items.gist: People in Austria gave more than a billion euros to charities last year. But organisations say rising costs mean each donated euro now does less.
items.summary: A report says people in Austria donated 1.08 billion euros in 2025. Private donations make up about 80 percent of funds for charitable work. The report says inflation has cut charities’ financial impact by about a quarter since 2023. Charity leaders say some households are reconsidering regular monthly gifts. Social and health services received the largest share of donations. The figures show both continued generosity and growing pressure on charities.
items.host_open: A billion euros is a generous total, but costs keep climbing. Do you think people will keep giving?

items.title: Ukraine Warns Of Winter Energy Attacks
items.gist: Ukraine says Russia may again target energy and transport systems as winter deepens. The warning comes while peace talks remain stuck over territory.
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia was preparing a major attack on energy infrastructure and other critical services. He urged partners to provide more air-defence weapons. US envoy Jared Kushner said talks with Russia had reached a deadlock over Ukrainian territory. Kushner also said Russian President Vladimir Putin had said he did not intend to use nuclear weapons. Ukrainian and European leaders say Moscow is still refusing to make compromises. Russia has not publicly confirmed the attack plans described by Zelenskyy.
items.host_open: For Ukrainians, a cold season makes power security especially important. How does this warning make you feel?

items.title: Israeli Strikes Kill Ten In Gaza
items.gist: Hospital officials in Gaza say Israeli strikes killed ten people. Israel says one strike targeted a Hamas official, while the military did not immediately comment on all reported attacks.
items.summary: Hospital officials said ten Palestinians were killed in several Israeli strikes and a shooting on Thursday. They said casualties included a man and his wife in an apartment in Deir al-Balah. Israel’s prime minister and defence minister said the military killed Hamas official Khaled Abu Nada. The Israeli military said one strike targeted three militants. It did not immediately respond to questions about other reported strikes. The deaths come despite a ceasefire agreement, as near-daily Israeli fire has continued.
items.host_open: Reports of more deaths in Gaza are deeply troubling. How do you feel about the latest developments?

items.title: Storm Leaves Hundreds Of Thousands Without Power
items.gist: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving across parts of the United States. Hundreds of thousands of customers lost electricity, and airports reported delays.
items.summary: About 820,000 US electricity customers were without power on Thursday afternoon, according to the outage tracker PowerOutage.us. Virginia, Maryland and Pennsylvania were among the hardest-hit states. A strong storm brought high winds and heavy rain to the East Coast. The National Weather Service had warned people about possible severe impacts. Flooding was reported in parts of Virginia. Airports in the Washington area saw delays and cancellations.
items.host_open: A holiday meal is less cosy when the lights go out. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Italy Sets Limits In Some School Classes
items.gist: Italy’s parliament has approved a limit on pupils with weak Italian-language skills in each class. The opposition says schools need more resources, not a quota.
items.summary: Italy’s parliament approved a law on school integration on Thursday. It sets a limit of 30 percent for pupils of foreign origin who do not speak enough Italian. The law also bans face-covering burkas in schools and requires parents to learn Italian. The government says the measures will support integration. Opposition leader Elly Schlein says schools need more investment, not limits that keep foreign children apart. The Senate had already approved the package.
items.host_open: A classroom can bring different languages together, but rules can divide opinion. What do you think?

items.title: Estonia Rejects Russian Border Accusations
items.gist: Russia has accused Estonia of hostile actions after the country closed a road border crossing. Estonia rejects the allegations and says Russia is the source of Europe’s security threats.
items.summary: Russia’s foreign ministry said Estonia’s border closure was one of several hostile actions. Moscow also accused Estonia of letting Ukraine use its airspace for attacks. Estonia’s foreign ministry said the country has never allowed its territory to be used for another state’s military operations. Russia also alleged that Estonia was trying to block Russian ships. There is no official naval blockade, according to the report. The dispute adds to tension between Russia and NATO member Estonia.
items.host_open: A border dispute can quickly become a wider security concern. How does this look from Austria?

items.title: Irish Court Blocks BAWAG Bank Deal
items.gist: An Irish court has rejected BAWAG’s planned takeover of Permanent TSB. The judge said minority shareholders did not get a separate vote required by law.
items.summary: Ireland’s High Court rejected BAWAG’s planned purchase of Permanent TSB, an Irish bank. The proposed deal was worth about 1.6 billion euros. The court said minority shareholders should have had a separate vote. The bank’s shareholders had already approved the deal in a wider vote. The judge said the court had to refuse approval because the legal requirement was not met. BAWAG said it was reviewing the decision, and it was not yet clear whether another vote could happen.
items.host_open: A cross-border bank deal has hit a legal roadblock. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Water Supplies Shrink Around The World
items.gist: A new study says the amount of water available worldwide has fallen sharply. Researchers link the change to hotter years and changes in how land stores water.
items.summary: A study reported a strong decline in water available around the world. Researchers examined changes in water held on land, including soil moisture and groundwater. They link the decline to a run of very hot years. The findings point to growing pressure on water supplies. The report says some regions are affected more than others. The research highlights a challenge for communities, farms and ecosystems.
items.host_open: Water is easy to take for granted until supplies fall. How does that make you feel?

items.title: Salzburg Keeps Europa League Hopes Alive
items.gist: Salzburg beat Ararat 2–0 at home in the Europa League. The win keeps the Austrian side in the race to reach the knockout stage.
items.summary: Red Bull Salzburg beat Armenian club Ararat 2–0 on Thursday. Bartosz Mazurek scored shortly after half-time. An own goal by Ararat’s Carlier made it 2–0 three minutes later. Salzburg had created many chances but struggled to score before the break. Salzburg coach Danny Röhl said his team needed to be more direct. The result gave Salzburg seven points and kept its hopes of advancing alive.
items.host_open: Two quick goals after the break made for a lively finish. Did that result surprise you?

items.title: Innsbruck Welcomes A Big-Air Comeback
items.gist: The Air & Style snowboarding event has returned to Innsbruck under a new name. Olympic champion Anna Gasser is taking part in the final season of her career.
items.summary: A new event called Airdrenaline has brought big-air snowboarding back to Innsbruck’s Bergisel hill. Anna Gasser is competing there for the first time. The two-time Olympic champion has said the 2026–27 season will be her last in the World Cup. Gasser qualified for Saturday’s final in fourth place. Freeskiers are also taking part at Bergisel for the first time. The event returned after years away from Innsbruck and has a history that includes a fatal crowd disaster in 1999.
items.host_open: A famous snowboarding event is back on a dramatic Innsbruck hill. Are you excited for the contest?

items.title: Seth Meyers Jokes About A Turkey Question
items.gist: A Thanksgiving turkey question became a topic in the latest late-night coverage. The news report says the president also spoke about a White House ballroom project.
items.summary: The Daily Beast reported that Seth Meyers joked about a question Donald Trump asked about a Thanksgiving turkey. The report said Trump used a turkey-pardoning event to discuss how large a bird was. It also said he spoke about his planned White House ballroom. Trump made a separate remark about Illinois Governor JB Pritzker at the event. The White House was contacted for comment by the publication. The underlying story came from a holiday event, not a policy announcement.
items.host_open: Thanksgiving brought an unusually memorable turkey question. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Judge Blocks FCC Action Against ABC
items.gist: A federal judge has stopped an early review of broadcast licences held by ABC stations. The administration’s regulator says it was acting within its authority; ABC says the action was retaliatory.
items.summary: A judge issued an injunction blocking the Federal Communications Commission from moving ahead with early reviews of eight ABC station licences. ABC had sued the FCC, arguing that the action was retaliation for its broadcasts. The regulator had raised concerns about possible violations of communications rules. The judge’s decision temporarily prevents those reviews from proceeding. The ruling is part of wider legal disputes between the administration and news organisations. The case does not settle all outstanding claims between the sides.
items.host_open: A court ruling has paused a regulator’s action against a broadcaster. How do you feel about that?
